citacoes.trecho: In this work, we focused on the main task of parallel code generation and conducted a systematic evaluation for the research questions discussed in Section V.

We address three research questions: assessing LLMs’ability to generate parallel code (RQ1), their capability to fix errors (RQ2), and the impact of different prompt designs on the quality of generated code (RQ3).
For each error type, we provided the LLM with The original problem statement, The erroneous code, and A description of the error (e.g., compiler output, runtime error message, or incorrect output).
P1: Contains only the problem statement and code signature.
P2: Contains P1 plus input-output examples.
P3: Contains P1 plus parallelization hints.
P4: Contains all components from the previous prompts.
These hints provide high-level guidance on the parallelization strategies for each parallel programming model.
We evaluated 100 randomly selected samples with 50 OpenMP and 50 MPI codes.
Incorporating parallelization hints consistently improves LLM performance in parallel code generation.
citacoes.localizador: p. 10 do PDF (impressa 555), Results and Observations

citacoes.trecho: Including all prompt components does not always result in better performance, suggesting the need for other prompt engineering techniques, such as chain-of-thought prompting.
citacoes.localizador: p. 10 do PDF (impressa 555), Results and Observations

citacoes.trecho: Works such as [22] show that LLMs may have seen many programming problems in their training datasets, and the data contamination will affect the performance of LLMs.
To ensure the integrity of our benchmark, we have rephrased problem statements and renamed functions and variables to use generic names.
This approach allows us to assess the model’s performance across multiple attempts, which is particularly relevant given the stochastic nature of LLM outputs.
This is crucial for parallel programming, as data races can lead to non-deterministic behavior and incorrect results.
citacoes.localizador: p. 5 do PDF (impressa 550), seção III-D, RaceFree@k

citacoes.trecho: We selected state-of-the-art general-purpose large language models such as GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4-turbo, and Gemini, alongside code-focused LLMs including CodeLlama and DeepSeek-Coder (33B).
For each problem in the benchmark, we generated k samples of parallel code, with k values set to 1, 5, and 10.
